content: 1. Anand Date, affiliated with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States, contributed to the development of these guidelines. 2. Lucia Gonzalez Fernandez, representing the International AIDS Society in Switzerland, also played a role in the creation of these guidelines. 3. Harry Hausler, from TBHIV Care in South Africa, provided expertise in the formulation of these recommendations. 4. Cecily Miller, associated with the University of California, San Francisco, contributed to the review and approval process. 5. Surbhi Modi, from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States, was involved in the development of these guidelines. 6. Suvanand Sahu, representing the Stop TB Partnership in Switzerland, participated in the review and approval of the guidelines. 7. Anna Scardigli, from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria in Switzerland, contributed to the process. The World Health Organization (WHO) acknowledges the contributions of the Guideline Review Committee and its WHO secretariat for their role in reviewing and approving the guidelines prior to publication. The 2020 update of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis (TB) preventive treatment was funded by grants provided to WHO by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the Russian Federation. The WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis preventive treatment, second edition, include the following abbreviations and acronyms: 1HP: One month of daily rifapentine plus isoniazid. 3HP: Three months of weekly rifapentine plus isoniazid. 3HR: Three months of daily rifampicin plus isoniazid. 4R: Four months of daily rifampicin monotherapy. 6H: Six months of daily isoniazid monotherapy. 6Lfx: Six months of daily levofloxacin. 9H: Nine months of daily isoniazid monotherapy. ART: Antiretroviral treatment. BCG: Bacille Calmette-Guérin (vaccine). CAD: Computer-aided detection. CI: Confidence interval. CRP: C-reactive protein. CXR: Chest radiography. ERG: External review group. GDG: Guideline Development Group. GRADE: Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. IGRA: Interferon-gamma release assay. IPT: Isoniazid preventive treatment (or monotherapy). LTBI: Latent tuberculosis infection. MDR-TB: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. mWRD: Molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic test. OR: Odds ratio. PICO: Population, intervention, comparator, and outcomes. PMTPT: Programmatic management of tuberculosis preventive treatment. RCT: Randomized controlled trial. RR: Relative risk. RR-TB: Rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis. TB: Tuberculosis. TBI: Tuberculosis infection. TBST: M. tuberculosis antigen-based skin test for TB infection. TNF: Tumor necrosis factor. TPT: Tuberculosis preventive treatment. TST: Tuberculin skin test. USA: United States of America. USAID: United States Agency for International Development. W4SS: WHO-recommended four-symptom screen. WHO: World Health Organization. Definitions used in these guidelines include: Active case finding (ACF): This refers to systematic screening for tuberculosis (TB) disease, typically conducted outside of healthcare facilities. Adolescent: A person aged 10–19 years. Adult: A person aged 19 years or older. Bacteriologically confirmed TB: TB diagnosed in a biological specimen through smear microscopy, culture, or a WHO-approved rapid diagnostic test such as Xpert® MTB/RIF or a urinary lipoarabinomannan assay. Child: A person aged less than 10 years. Contact: Any individual who has been exposed to a person with TB disease. Contact investigation: The systematic identification of undiagnosed TB disease and TB infection among contacts of an index case or in settings where transmission occurs. This includes clinical evaluation, testing, and provision of appropriate anti-TB therapy or TB preventive treatment (TPT). High TB transmission setting: A setting with a high frequency of undetected or undiagnosed TB disease, or where infectious TB patients are present, increasing the risk of TB transmission. Household contact: A person who shared the same enclosed living space as the index case for one or more nights or for frequent or extended daytime periods during the three months prior to the start of current treatment. Index person with TB: The initially identified individual with new or recurrent TB in a specific household or comparable setting where others may have been exposed. Infant: A child aged less than one year (12 months). People who use drugs: Individuals engaging in harmful or hazardous use of psychoactive substances, negatively affecting their health, social life, resources, or legal situation. Programmatic management of TB preventive treatment (PMTPT): Coordinated activities by public and private healthcare providers and the community to provide TPT to those in need. Skin test: Intradermal inoculation of tuberculin (TST) or M. tuberculosis antigen (TBST) to elicit a response indicative of TB infection. Tuberculosis (TB): The disease state caused by M. tuberculosis, referred to as TB disease in this document to distinguish it from TB infection. Tuberculosis infection (TBI): A state of persistent immune response to stimulation by M. tuberculosis antigens without clinically manifest TB disease. Most infected individuals show no signs or symptoms of TB but remain at risk of developing TB disease. The WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of TB preventive treatment (TPT) as a key intervention to achieve the End TB Strategy targets. TPT is part of a broader framework of preventive actions, including TB screening, infection control, and care for individuals with HIV and other comorbidities.
